gap_rows.title: rwb-integration credit approval pack: login, contract field names, NLEADS read, the ownership split, the integration-base resource placement and the approval-level values are not settled by any one source
gap_rows.source: WP B-P2-02; legacy RWB-E2-006; Ownership Map v1; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 and A1.5; TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 and T-A.1/T-A.2 (API-P2-012, API-P2-013 retired); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 16, 41 and 43; RWB-P3-E2006-APP
gap_rows.description: One combined gap covers everything this slice cannot read from a single source. (1) The rwb-integration login name (DP-02) is given nowhere; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login. (2) The exact JSON field names of the contracts this slice consumes are given nowhere: the rwb-source-data account, collateral, freshness and NLEADS credit-decision reads; the rwb-treatment plan-terms read and credit-result record; the rwb-document checklist read; the rwb-case read, action and reference-data read; and the rwb-access delegation and authorise answers. (3) The NLEADS credit-decision operation and its field shape do not exist in any source: TSD P2 v3 API-P2-012 reads v_ace_credit_decision in P2, while DP-05 and Architecture v5 slide 41 make rwb-source-data the only reader of the ACE views, and the tier 2 view waits on DL43. (4) The ownership split is a split of one legacy story across four owners and is fixed only by the plan and the Ownership Map: the case-side pack, the route state, the queue and the case-side record are rwb-case's (RWB-P3-E2006-APP); the four treatment columns nleads_ref, credit_result, credit_result_reason and credit_result_at and the treatment state are rwb-treatment's (S2 story of this key); the delegation of authority is rwb-access's (P4) and the approval routing P7's; the two integration-base resources stay with rwb-integration. The split makes the same pack composed twice, case-side and integration-side, and makes one decision produce a record at each owner, neither of which any source settles. (5) The placement of the two resources conflicts across sources: the Ownership Map keeps both with P2 (the GET on API Specification v4, the POST on v2 and absent from v3 and v4), TSD P2 v3 retires the result operation as API-P2-013 and removes the four treatment columns, FSD P2 v3 is outbound-file only and puts NLEADS out of scope, and the Architecture v5 service contract slide lists only GET /interface-runs, POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, FileDelivered and FileFailed for P2. (6) The new request and response shapes on the integration base are taken from the legacy CreditPack and CreditResult shapes because no contract fixes the JSON form, the error body or the header set beyond If-Match and Idempotency-Key. (7) The input age limit of 1 business day for balances is a legacy assumption (DL22) and is read as a reference row. (8) The approval-level values in the legacy criteria are inconsistent: AC2 records level L5 for a plan the Background puts at L6 or higher, and AC7 refuses level L6 for a plan that needs L5; both are copied unchanged, the comparison rule (at or above the level rwb-access returns) is applied, and the values are left to the delegation owner.
gap_rows.evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 3 (input age limit 1 business day, assumed, DL22), Background (plan needs L6 or higher), AC2 (approval level L5), AC7 (L6 refused for a plan that needs L5), section 12 (CreditPack and CreditResult shapes, CaseEvents.raise, DelegationQuery, TreatmentCommands, CaseDocuments) and section 13 (feature flag rwb.integration.nleads-pack, four new treatment columns); Ownership Map v1: GET /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-pack owner P2, POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result owner P2 on API Specification v2 and absent from v3 and v4, delegation_limit owner P4, treatment owner S2, reference_row and recovery_case owner P3; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 (in scope: outbound adapters only) and A1.1 out of scope (NLEADS lands in ACE and is read through the views); TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 (v_ace_credit_decision, tier 2, read by API-P2-012), T-A.1 API-P2-012 (credit-pack) and API-P2-013 (retired, four treatment columns removed); Architecture v5 slide 16 rwb-integration IN REST GET /interface-runs and POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry, OUT FileDelivered and FileFailed, slide 41 (rwb_integration owns interface config, file runs, outbound items, ACE integration paths), slide 43 (FileDelivered, FileFailed on rwb.integration.events.v1) and slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s); no source names the rwb-integration login, the contract field names, the reference-data read path or the SCR-14 composite route
gap_rows.proposed: Settle in the wave 2 contract review: the rwb-integration login with the ACE DB owner; the two resources' placement in the Service Contract Catalog, with the P2 catalogue line and the retirement entry of the technical specification reconciled; the operation names and field sets of the rwb-source-data NLEADS read, the rwb-treatment result record, the rwb-case read, action and reference-data read, and the rwb-access delegation answer; one owner for the pack composition on SCR-14 and one record owner per decision; the reference-data read path; and the AC2 and AC7 approval levels against doa.txt item 2.1.1. Record the outcome in the contract stories and the gap and assumption registers; no business value changes in this story.

asm_rows.text: The rwb-integration service runs as one login created with the rwb_integration schema by the platform DB work (DP-02); the story names it "the rwb-integration login" until the name is agreed.
asm_rows.why: No source gives the login name, and every DP-02 row requires one login per service; the legacy story ran on the shared recovery_svc login.
asm_rows.read: RWB-P2-E2006-APP sections 3, 10 and 13; DP-02 in Template and Rules section R5.5; Architecture v5 slide 41 (one schema and one login per service).
asm_rows.confirm: ACE DB owner and the platform DB story, before the rwb_integration baseline is created
asm_rows.impact: None on behaviour: the login is named by role in the story and swapped for the agreed name without a content change.

asm_rows.text: The two treatment-scoped operations of the legacy story, the credit-pack read and the credit-result write, stay with rwb-integration under the integration base /api/recovery/integration/v1, as the Ownership Map records, although the P2 functional specification is outbound-file only, the P2 technical specification retires the result operation, and the Architecture v5 service contract slide lists only the interface-run resources for P2.
asm_rows.why: Three sources disagree. The Ownership Map keeps both operations with P2 on the strength of the API Specification v4 GET form and the v2 POST form, the legacy story calls both P2 Integration endpoints, and the P3 story of the same legacy key leaves them to the P2 slice; the alternative, moving them to rwb-case, would put the NLEADS submission step on the case owner and duplicate the case-side pack a second time.
asm_rows.read: Ownership Map v1 (GET /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-pack owner P2; POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result owner P2, basis API Specification v2, absent from v3 and v4); Architecture v5 slide 16 (P2 IN: GET /interface-runs, POST /interface-runs/{id}/retry; OUT: FileDelivered, FileFailed) and slide 41; FSD P2 Integration v3 A1.1 (in scope: outbound adapters only) and A1.1 out of scope (NLEADS); TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.2 API-P2-012 and API-P2-013 (retired).
asm_rows.confirm: Solution architect at the Service Contract Catalog review, with the P2 and P3 owners
asm_rows.impact: If the operations move, the two paths and the base change and the pack and result tests move with them; no behaviour changes.

asm_rows.text: The NLEADS credit decision is read through the rwb-source-data contract over v_ace_credit_decision and returns the NLEADS reference, the result, the approval level, the result date and the reason for a refusal, keyed by the plan of the treatment; this service reads no ACE view.
asm_rows.why: TSD P2 v3 API-P2-012 reads v_ace_credit_decision in P2 directly, but DP-05 and Architecture v5 slide 41 make rwb-source-data the only reader of the ACE views, and no source gives the operation name or the field shape.
asm_rows.read: TSD P2 Integration v3 T1.1 (v_ace_credit_decision, tier 2, read by API-P2-012) and T-A.2 API-P2-012; Architecture v5 slide 15 (P1 owns the ACE view contract and freshness) and slide 41; DP-05 in Template and Rules section R5.5; RWB-P2-E2006-APP section 12.2.
asm_rows.confirm: Source-data owner (RWB-P1 contract stories) and ACE, before wave 2 build, and DL43 for the tier 2 view
asm_rows.impact: The result record cites the ACE row instead of a re-keyed value; the operation name and field names may change without a behaviour change.

asm_rows.text: The credit-pack response keeps the legacy CreditPack field set (caseNo, productGroup, accounts with accountNo, principal, interest, totalBalance, daysPastDue, dataAsOf and ageDays, collateral with collateralNo, type, appraisedValue and appraisalDate, terms with offerAmount, haircutAmount, installments and validUntil, requiredLevel, documents with type plus documentId or missing, and messages) and the credit-result request keeps the legacy CreditResult field set (nleadsRef, result, approvalLevel, resultDate, reason) with If-Match; the JSON field names of the source-data, treatment, document, case and access contracts are the ones those two shapes imply and the field-level reviews confirm.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story fixes the two integration-base shapes and no source fixes the contract field names they are filled from; the story cannot be built or contract-tested without a default.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 12 (both endpoints, the CreditPack and CreditResult shapes and the errors); TSD P2 Integration v3 T-A.2 API-P2-012 (CreditPack); Architecture v5 slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1 contract-first, one hop); RWB-P2-E2006-APP section 12.1 and section 12.2.
asm_rows.confirm: Contract owner of RWB-P3-E2004-CON and the source-data, document and access contract owners at the contract review
asm_rows.impact: A renamed field touches one client and one fake; no business value changes.

asm_rows.text: The case is read through the rwb-case contract by case reference, and CREDIT_APPROVED or CREDIT_DECLINED is raised through the case action operation of that contract with the reference, the final call and the freshness; this slice publishes no business event and adds no topic.
asm_rows.why: The legacy CaseEvents.raise call was in process (DP-11) and Architecture v5 gives rwb-case the case and CMMN state and no P2 topic, so the raise has to be an operation or an event, and this slice is not given the outbox and topic library of DP-09.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 12 (CaseEvents.raise); Architecture v5 slide 14 (rwb-case IN: POST /cases/{id}/actions) and slide 16 (P2 OUT: FileDelivered, FileFailed only); DP-11 and DP-09 in Template and Rules section R5.5.
asm_rows.confirm: Case owner (RWB-P3-E2006-APP and the case contract) with the solution architect
asm_rows.impact: If the raise becomes an event, the client changes and the build gains the outbox and topic library as a dependency; the behaviour does not change.

asm_rows.text: The input age limit for the balances in a credit pack is 1 business day, read as a reference row of the owning reference data rather than written in code; the legacy story records it as an assumption under DL22.
asm_rows.why: No source fixes the value and the legacy story states it as an assumption, so it must not become a constant in the service.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 3 (the input age limit for balances in a credit pack is 1 business day, assumed, DL22) and section 13; RWB-P2-E2006-APP section 3, section 12.7 and section 13.
asm_rows.confirm: Business lead at the pack rules review
asm_rows.impact: The limit may change without a release; the story behaviour is unaffected.

asm_rows.text: The recorded approval level must be at or above the level the rwb-access delegation contract returns for decision D5, the product group and the amount; the legacy values are copied unchanged, including level "L5" recorded in AC2 against a plan the Background sets at "L6" or higher and level "L6" refused in AC7 for a plan that needs "L5".
asm_rows.why: The two legacy statements cannot both be right, and neither may be corrected in a copy of the criteria; the comparison rule itself is clear, while the values are not.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-006 Background and AC2 (L5 recorded), AC7 (L6 refused for a plan that needs L5), BR5 and MSG-P2-018; doa.txt item 2.1.1 as cited by the legacy story; RWB-P2-E2006-APP section 7 and section 16.
asm_rows.confirm: Business lead and Risk (delegation owner) before wave 2 build
asm_rows.impact: If the legacy values are wrong, the two test fixtures are corrected and the story text follows; the comparison logic does not change.

asm_rows.text: The NLEADS pack checklist rows are read through the rwb-case reference-data contract with the version in force, as five rows for the legacy items CREDIT_APPLICATION, ID_COPY, TITLE_DEED, LATEST_APPRAISAL and INCOME_PROOF.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story holds the checklist as reference data and names the five assumed items, and DP-07 moves reference data to rwb-case; no source gives the read path or the row identifiers.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 3 (checklist items), BR6 and section 13 (NLEADS pack checklist rows, DL19); DP-07 in Template and Rules section R5.5; RWB-P2-E2006-APP section 12.2.
asm_rows.confirm: Reference-data owner (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and the business lead, DL19
asm_rows.impact: The row set and its version are data; a change of the checklist changes no code.

asm_rows.text: This slice writes its own decision record with decision "D5" in rwb_integration in the same local transaction as the acceptance, before any remote call, and the case-side record with the route state and the treatment-side state and columns are written by their owners, so the same decision is recorded at each owner and sealed in order by the central ledger.
asm_rows.why: DP-03 writes the record locally in the owning service in the same transaction as its own change, and the split puts one change in each of three services; no source states how many records one decision produces or in which order the ledger seals them.
asm_rows.read: Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 15, 16 and 28 (local record, same transaction, hash chain, central ledger); DP-03 in Template and Rules section R5.5; legacy RWB-E2-006 section 4 steps 8 and 9 and AC11; RWB-P3-E2006-APP section 12.3.
asm_rows.confirm: Risk and Internal Audit at the ADR-009 review, with the rwb-decision ledger owner
asm_rows.impact: If one record per decision is required, the record is written once by the case owner and this slice keeps only the acceptance; the blocking rule and the incident are unchanged.

asm_rows.text: SCR-14 reaches the two integration-base operations through the gateway-bff composite route, which also calls the case-side pack of rwb-case in parallel and merges the two answers, preferring the case-side value where both carry the same field.
asm_rows.why: The legacy screen was served by the monolith; in the target the screen is served at the edge and the pack is now composed twice, case-side and integration-side, and no source fixes the route or the merge.
asm_rows.read: Architecture v5 slides 10 and 12 (BFF composes a few parallel calls, one hop each, merge at the BFF); DP-19 in Template and Rules section R5.5; RWB-P2-E2006-APP section 15; RWB-P3-E2006-APP section 15.
asm_rows.confirm: Edge and gateway owner (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) with the screen design
asm_rows.impact: The merge rule and the route fields may change; the two operations and their fields do not.

asm_rows.text: The legacy feature flag name rwb.integration.nleads-pack is kept as the legacy reference only; the switch is a feature flag of the platform flag library, and when it is off the result operation is refused with MSG-GEN-006 while nothing is written and the pack is hidden from the composite route.
asm_rows.why: The legacy story names the flag in P2 code, and the platform default ruling moves feature flags to the platform library; the story needs a defined off behaviour.
asm_rows.read: Legacy RWB-E2-006 section 13 (feature flag name); Template and Rules section R3 default ruling (feature flags to the platform library) and section R5.5 DP-15; Ownership Map v1 (feature_flag owner PLT).
asm_rows.impact: The flag key and its off behaviour are configuration; no business value changes.
